headline: IN-WINDOW UPDATE TO 0400-01
dek: Saudi Civil Defence has lifted the early-warning alert for Riyadh that it activated at 03:54 (0400-01). The liveblog entry gives no cause, threat type, intercept, damage or casualty detail for the Riyadh alert itself; the all-clear closes the alert, it does not explain it.
sources: Saudi General Directorate of Civil Defence announcement, relayed by Al Jazeera Nov 4 liveblog
fault_line: All-clear without explanation: routine precaution or a threat Riyadh is not naming?

sections.what_happened: Saudi Civil Defence has lifted the early-warning alert for Riyadh that it activated at 03:54 (0400-01). The liveblog entry gives no cause, threat type, intercept, damage or casualty detail for the Riyadh alert itself; the all-clear closes the alert, it does not explain it.
sections.what_verified: Official announcement relayed by AJ liveblog; no second outlet relay found in-window. The 0400-01 activation is corroborated by the @saudinews50 graphic (03:49 ) and the AJ 23:54 GMT entry.
sections.what_disputed: None: no source disputes the lift. The gap is the missing cause — no coalition statement in-window attributes the Riyadh alert to a specific launch, and no intercept over Riyadh was claimed for this alert (contrast the Nov 2 Riyadh two-drone intercept, a separate event).
sections.why_matters: Riyadh alert ends as quietly as it began — the capital's warning system, not a strike, is the story; do not inflate into an attack claim.
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW UPDATE TO 0400-01: Saudi Civil Defence lifts the Riyadh early-warning alert (AJ liveblog 00:06 GMT = 04:06 )

totw_analysis: Our read: Riyadh alert ends as quietly as it began — the capital's warning system, not a strike, is the story; do not inflate into an attack claim. The fault line our audience is arguing over: All-clear without explanation: routine precaution or a threat Riyadh is not naming?
